name: hMOF-7001666
vfSrc: RASPA helium on this CIF; metadata says 0.627
pill: Descriptor mismatch, not a label error
text: A different kind of problem. The metadata describes an open pore (void fraction 0.627, LCD 9.25 Å, PLD 7.25 Å), but the CIF is dense: helium void fraction 0.119, LCD 3.7 Å, PLD 1.5 Å, density 1.65 g/cm³. GCMC on the CIF gives 7.71 and 12.0 g/L, close to the labels (7.64 and 9.47). So the uptake labels fit the structure; it's the geometric descriptors that belong to something else. It was flagged only because the floor used the wrong void fraction. Running it in the reference 2×2×2 box gave the same 12.0 g/L.

name: ZIF-1 (teaching)
tag: Closed cages · GCMC fills cages H₂ can't reach
ff: Teaching run: UFF + three-site Darkrim–Levesque H₂, no Feynman–Hibbs
pill: Uptake in cages H₂ cannot reach
text: Kept from the first round to show one limitation of GCMC. The windows (1.9 Å) are narrower than H₂, yet standard GCMC inserts molecules directly into the cages and reports 18.3 and 26.1 g/L. With the cages blocked, uptake is 0.0 g/L. This matters for small-pore hMOFs: whether a label counts H₂ in unreachable cages depends on whether pocket blocking was used.

name: ZIF-1, cages blocked

ff: Teaching run: UFF + three-site Darkrim–Levesque H₂, no Feynman–Hibbs
text: Identical settings with every cage that H₂ cannot reach blocked. Uptake drops to 0.0 g/L at both pressures.
